batch_selection: Order the new OpenCS cohort's native IRIs by SHA-256 of 0.7.0-topics followed by NUL and the IRI. Take five.

cases.rationale: The native topic label, parent and explicit referent agree with the reviewed scope. A first-order formula with existential quantifiers eliminated using fresh Skolem functions or constants, leaving a universal quantifier prefix, in the usual satisfiability-preserving transformation.

The native topic label, parent and explicit referent agree with the reviewed scope. A primitive recursive relation witnessing that a code records a terminating computation for the given program and input.

The native topic label, parent and explicit referent agree with the reviewed scope. The least nonrecursive ordinal, equivalently the supremum of the order types of computable well-orderings of the natural numbers.
The native topic label, parent and explicit referent agree with the reviewed scope. An effective encoding of syntactic objects such as formulas and derivations by natural numbers.
The native topic label, parent and explicit referent agree with the reviewed scope. An idempotent semiring equipped with a star operation satisfying star-unfolding and induction axioms.
Differentiability of both factors at x is explicit in the canonical scope.
The expression guard selects half-integer nonintegers; the consequence states evenness.
The function is a real probability density with a finite absolute first moment, and the published integral retains that scope.
The power applies to the displacement from the center. The integral requires a finite moment and specified order.
The native operation uses addition of multiplicities and distributes over pointwise minimum.
Proper subset occurs only in the guard. The reviewed claim is a direction from proper inclusion to ordinary inclusion and distinctness.
The interval symbol is missing from the pinned dictionary. The expression remains rejected even though the intended additivity statement is familiar.
The reference spells less-than-or-equal as relation1:le; the dictionary declares leq.
Set cardinality collapses duplicate values, so the witness gives the wrong denominator for a sample with repetitions.
The source expression lacks a square root and supplies the density in the role of an outcome.
The displayed source expression negates the exponential value instead of negating the exponent.
The source axiom has an existential algorithm filler for an implementation class. The reviewed topic refers to the algorithm it realizes.
The run and implementation have distinct activity and executable roles.
The source existential restricts the modeled class and the canonical statement documents the output role scoped to that model.
The result refers to a measure, which has a separate identity from its value or computation.
The scope admits an assessment procedure as one role of a specification.
The scope admits a measure as a separate role of the assessment specification.
This source occurrence assigns a parameter role to the same property. Performance measurement requires a separate witness.
This output represents a trained model. An evaluation-result claim requires the separate evaluation filler.
The pinned proof counts observations. Its probability interpretation explicitly requires a nonempty multiset.
A set of distinct observations omits frequencies and cannot witness this denominator.
The declaration has two derivative hypotheses and corroborates the ordinary product rule through real specialization.
The source proof uses a parameterized extensional fixed-point theorem and establishes the scoped Rice result.
The source uses equality of evaluated partial functions. Code identity calls for different evidence.
The source uses the append equation on finite words, with the intermediate state passed to the second evaluation.
The pinned historical representation assigns the two masses to true and false, including the degenerate endpoint values.
The equivalence identifies the coordinates used in the representation and gives a map back to complex numbers.
The explicit referent and lambda-calculus parents corroborate the existing Curry–Howard topic.
The alternate fixed-point topic supports a close mapping alongside the separately evidenced recursion-theorem topic.
The OWL class names the complex plane. The canonical subject concerns its mathematical representation rather than class equivalence.
Mathematical logic has a relevant native OWL class; the canonical logic topic is an editorial subject.
A Welch t statistic and a t reference law have separate roles, even though the native input predicate covers both.
The variable-importance-in-projection score is a fitted PLS diagnostic rather than a statistical parameter estimate.
The normality assumption does not supply the null law of the Dixon spacing ratio.
Continuity of the null observation distribution does not specify the test statistic's sampling law.

selection_limit: The audit samples the new cohort and separately targets expression, mapping, and proof roles. The outcome counts do not estimate a graph-wide error rate.

cso.explanation: The workspace fetch returned HTTP 403. Shared-anchor review uses explicit sameAs witnesses from approved CSO decisions and the pinned OpenCS snapshot.

mathlib4.explanation: Textual headers and reviewed declaration ranges are indexed. Elaboration and extraction of kernel proof dependencies require a pinned Lean environment.

ontomath-edu.explanation: The pinned native OWL artifacts remain available in staging pending verification of publication rights.

ontomath-pro.explanation: The source restriction inventory counts universal and existential forms separately. A reviewed OWL class reference guides reconciliation while the independent Mathlib witness supplies the coordinate equivalence.

opencs.explanation: The full eligible neighborhood counts and shared anchor review retain SKOS meanings. Cohort admission separately checks the source label, anchor and native parent.

openmath.explanation: Selected dictionaries require the approved derivative-work notice. Unresolved native symbols, missing bindings and semantic rejections retain distinct review states.
